body: Two foundational aspects of human cognition, abstractness and gender, are typically examined as separable. Here, we find they are systematically linked throughout the entire space of concepts spanning single (N = 40,000) and multi-word expressions (N = 67,000): across billions of words and millions of images on the internet -- and across numerous measurement techniques -- more abstract concepts are more associated with men, an effect which replicates in languages around the world. This pattern not only holds across conceptual domains, but it also maps onto grammatical structure: verbs and adverbs are more abstract and more male-coded, a system-wide trace of stereotypes accentuating agentic qualities in men. Furthermore, this bias emerges in human and AI responses in free association tasks, indicating its internalization and its algorithmic reproduction. The male abstraction bias may underlie and unify a range of stereotypes, evidencing gender as a core organizing dimension in conceptual space.
summaryZh: 互联网文化和大型语言模型中的男性抽象偏见。人类认知的两个基本方面，抽象性和性别，通常被视为可分离的。在这里，我们发现它们在跨越单个词（N = 40,000）和多词表达（N = 67,000）的整个概念空间中系统地联系在一起：跨越互联网上的数十亿个单词和数百万张图像——以及无数的测量技术——更抽象的概念与男性的联系更紧密，这种效应在世界各地的语言中都得到了复制。
